title: Somerset Council: Using Microsoft Copilot to improve productivity
summary: Somerset Council reports that Microsoft Copilot saved pilot users two to four hours a week and that 75% reported better focus and 53% found work more enjoyable.
account: Somerset offered 300 Copilot licenses to staff and assessed their experiences after three months. Staff reportedly reduced meeting-minute work from 72 to 17 minutes and saved two to four hours weekly. Productivity and enjoyment results are self-reported. The stated 4–10x ROI is project-side valuation, not independently validated cash savings. The council launched the pilot in November 2023 and took its results from a review in February 2024. It also reported that some volunteers returned their licenses and that Microsoft's usage dashboards were inaccurate. In a later pilot with a control group, the Department for Business and Trade found that Copilot saved small amounts of time and helped neurodiverse staff, but it found no evidence that the savings improved productivity.
purpose: Explore whether Copilot improves staff productivity and work experience.

data.answer:
Somerset reports two to four hours saved weekly per Copilot user, with 75% reporting better focus and 53% finding work more enjoyable.

The results rely heavily on user feedback and lack a randomized comparison or reported response denominator. Valuing two to four hours against license cost does not establish cash savings or net ROI after support, checking, and implementation costs. Returned licenses and acknowledged usage-dashboard inaccuracies qualify the positive reports.
